title: Shafarevich-Tate groups of holomorphic Lagrangian fibrations II

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The theorem says that 'the following are equivalent:' but the three numbered statements are absent. The proof nevertheless refers to '(1) ⇒ (2)', '(2) ⇒ (3)', and '(3) ⇒ (1)'. Thus the theorem has no stated content and cannot establish the claimed projectivity criterion in Theorem A(2), including the non-torsion direction.

The claimed 'natural isomorphism' NS_Q(X)/eta -> NS_Q(X^phi)/eta is not proved. The construction only associates, after taking unspecified powers, a line bundle L^phi to an individual line bundle L. It does not prove independence from the representative in NS_Q, additivity, independence from choices of cocycle/trivializations beyond a base pullback, or that the resulting map has an inverse. Step 3 establishes preservation of relative ampleness only conditional on the construction, not that the claimed map is an isomorphism.

The proof asserts that a line bundle K' on S' (whose complement has codimension at least two) can always be extended to a line bundle K on an arbitrary variety S. This is false without additional assumptions such as suitable smoothness/factoriality. On a normal non-factorial singular variety, a line bundle on the smooth/codimension-one locus can extend only as a rank-one reflexive sheaf, not as an invertible sheaf. The lemma is stated for arbitrary varieties and is subsequently used when the base may be singular.

The proposition has no actual conclusion: immediately after its hypotheses it contains the text 'Step 2. The manifold Y contains ... The statement is proven.' before the proof begins. This is apparently an outline fragment rather than a proposition statement. Corollary 4.4.3 then invokes Proposition 4.4.2 for the unstated claim that Y admits a Lagrangian fibration bimeromorphic to that on X, so a necessary result is formally missing.

The key linear-algebra assertion is false: 'a real subspace of a complex vector space which is Lagrangian with respect to a holomorphic symplectic form is complex.' For example, in C^2 with holomorphic symplectic form dz1∧dz2, the real plane spanned by ∂/∂x1 and ∂/∂x2 is a real Lagrangian/isotropic plane but is not invariant under the complex structure. Consequently, the argument that the real-analytic graph Gamma automatically becomes a complex analytic subvariety of X_t×Y_t fails, invalidating the claimed bimeromorphism f_t and the later use of this proposition.

An unexplained embedded JPEG/base64 image is inserted into the mathematical proof. It has no caption explaining mathematical content, no citation in the surrounding argument, and is not referenced except by the generated label 'Figure 0'. It is plainly unrelated to the stated proof and constitutes document/figure corruption that must be removed or replaced.

The attempted proof that sigma^r is not bar-partial exact uses the expression ∫_X sigma^n sigma^n != 0. On a complex manifold of dimension 2n, sigma^n is already a holomorphic top-degree (2n,0)-form, so sigma^n∧sigma^n has type (4n,0) and is identically zero; it cannot yield the asserted nonzero integral. The preceding expression involving alpha sigma^{n-r} sigma^n also has incompatible bidegree. Thus the displayed contradiction is invalid.

After proving a statement about sections of R^2 pi_* Z and local Chern classes of line bundles, the text concludes: 'In particular, every section xi of R^1 pi_* Z is locally the class of a closed (1,1)-form.' This has the wrong cohomological degree: a closed (1,1)-form represents a degree-two class, not a section of R^1. It must at least read R^2 pi_* Z; as written the claimed consequence is false.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 5.3.9, statement versus its proof and Theorem C
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proposition says that b2(X^phi)=b2(X) occurs iff there is a class h in H^2(X) restricting nontrivially to a smooth fiber. But X is the original hyperkähler manifold and always has such a class (e.g. a Kähler class, whose fiber restriction is ample), which would make the first case always occur. The proof instead correctly uses a class in H^2(X^phi), and Theorem C also states the condition for X^phi. The proposition's stated criterion is therefore false and contradicts the surrounding results.
